questions.questionText: Analyze Shakespeare's depiction of vaulting ambition and psychological guilt in Macbeth. Support with textual references.
questions.referenceAnswer: Macbeth examines how hubris and prophetic temptation override moral conscience. Key soliloquies ("If it were done when 'tis done", "Tomorrow and tomorrow") reveal internal descent into paranoia, echoed by Lady Macbeth's somnambulism ("Out, damned spot").
expectedConcepts: Psychological decay of Macbeth and Lady Macbeth
acceptableAlternatives: Aristotelian tragic flaw interpretation or political Jacobean allegory
markingCriteria: 3 marks for literary analysis of dramatic irony and imagery

questions.questionText: Explain the socioeconomic and institutional causes of the French Revolution of 1789.
questions.referenceAnswer: Causes include: 1) Three Estates feudal inequality with Third Estate bearing tax burden (taille), 2) Financial insolvency from Seven Years War and American Revolution, 3) Agricultural famine of 1788-1789, 4) Enlightenment ideals (Rousseau, Voltaire) challenging absolutism.
acceptableAlternatives: Marxist class struggle analysis or revisionist fiscal-institutional interpretation
markingCriteria: 3 marks for social structure & Estates General
